Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

carefully adverb

cautiously, so as not to fall, break or hurt

also cautiously, warily, gingerly, step by step

classical

Plaut. Trin. 2.2.46: cautē et cōgitātē rem tractāre (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Clu. 118 (Lewis & Short)

cautē

adverb

carefully, cautiously, warily

From cautus, wary (caveō, beware): with care against danger or mistakes. In Cicero also “with proper security”, of a thing done with guarantees (Lewis & Short). To warn someone, say cavē nē … (see careful, don’t fall).

Other words

  • pedetemptim (pedetentim) — step by step, cautiously

    adverb · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 4.2.32: Pedetemptim. (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fam. 9.14.7: pedetemptim et gradātim (Lewis & Short)

    Literally “feeling one’s way with the feet”: slowly, a step at a time, and so “cautiously, by degrees” (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • cautē et cōgitātē rem tractāre

    to handle the matter carefully and thoughtfullyPlaut. Trin. 2.2.46 (Lewis & Short)

  • In viā pergit cautē (prōvidē), nē impingat aut aberret.

    She goes along the road carefully, so as not to stumble or lose her way.Comen. OP 110

  • Pōculum cautē portā; vitreum est.

    Carry the cup carefully; it’s glass.composed

See also carefully, careful, don’t fall, slowly, watch out!.
